content.label: Chemistry only - why reactivity falls down Group 7
content.body: Halogens react by gaining one electron into their outer shell. Down the group the incoming electron feels less attraction: the atom is bigger and its outer shell is further from the nucleus and screened by more inner shells. So fluorine grabs electrons best and is the most reactive - the opposite direction to Group 1, where the electron lost is held more weakly as atoms grow.
